# End-to-end tests (Layer 3)

These scenarios drive the real application (`main.py`, an actual subprocess)
through [pywinauto](https://pywinauto.readthedocs.io/) (UIA backend), against a
**synthetic, disposable** photo library generated by
`tools/test_env/generate_library.py`, with a `%LOCALAPPDATA%` **isolated** from
the user's real profile (see `tools/test_env/launch_isolated.py`).

No test in this folder touches the real catalog, config, thumbnails or face
database. The application's default export folder
(`~/Pictures/PixelPhotoManager/Export`) is explicitly overridden in
`test_export.py` for the same reason — never remove that override.

## Requirements

Windows only. `pywinauto` is **not** in `requirements.txt` (Layers 1+2, which
are cross-platform): it is a separate, optional dependency.

```powershell
.venv\Scripts\pip.exe install -r requirements-test-e2e.txt
```

Without `pywinauto` installed, `tests/e2e/conftest.py` automatically drops
`scenarios/*` from collection (`collect_ignore_glob`) — `pytest tests/` keeps
working normally (Layers 1+2 only).

## Running the scenarios

```powershell
# Every scenario (slow: each test launches a real instance of the application,
# full scan and InsightFace face indexing included — several minutes)
.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pytest tests/e2e -m e2e -v

# A single scenario
.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pytest tests/e2e/scenarios/test_duplicate_detection.py -m e2e -v
```

`pytest tests/` (the default command documented in `CLAUDE.md`) does **not**
run these scenarios: `pytest.ini` sets `addopts = -m "not e2e"`. You always
need `-m e2e` (or `-m ""` to include everything) to trigger them.

## Code coverage of the scenarios

`--cov` does not see code executed by the application (a subprocess). To make
the scenarios credit coverage of the UI code:

```powershell
$env:PPM_E2E_COVERAGE='1'
.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pytest tests/e2e -m e2e
.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m coverage combine
.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m coverage report
```

`launch_isolated.py` then starts the application through `coverage run` (one
`.coverage.<host>.<pid>` file per launch, cf. `parallel = true` in
`.coveragerc`), and `_graceful_close()` (conftest) closes the window cleanly
before the fallback `terminate()` — a TerminateProcess would not run the atexit
hook that writes the data out. This report combines only the code executed by
the 14 e2e scenarios (not the baseline `pytest tests/` suite): the overall
total (46%) is **normally below the `fail_under` ratchet** (49), so
`coverage report` returns a non-zero exit code in this mode — that is expected,
purely informational, never gating. Orders of magnitude observed with the
current 14 scenarios (2026-07): `main_window.py` 73%, `thumbnail_grid.py` 72%,
`edit_panel.py` 70%, `photo_viewer.py` 69%, `sidebar.py` 70%,
`face_cluster_grid.py` 55%, `main_window_faces.py` 47% — a clear rise compared
to the ~35%/~49% (`main_window.py`/`thumbnail_grid.py`) measured with the two
initial tests of `test_scan_and_browse.py` alone.

## What each scenario checks

| File | Checks |
|---|---|
| `test_scan_and_browse.py` | Automatic scan at startup (no onboarding, `config.json` pre-filled) → every synthetic photo catalogued, `media_type` correct. Corrupted file: the scan must not crash (exact outcome not pinned down — a point to enrich). |
| `test_duplicate_detection.py` | **Flagship scenario** — a direct regression test for the `Signal(dict)`-with-int-keys bug fixed in 2026-07 (see `bugfix_signal_dict_int_keys_2026-07.md`): the detection now starts automatically after the scan, so the test waits on it (`wait_for_duplicate_detection`) and then asserts on `duplicate_group_id` in the database. Covers Tier 1 (pHash: exact and resized pairs) and Tier 2 (ORB/RANSAC: cropped pair). |
| `test_duplicates_ui.py` | UI actions on duplicates, complementing the DB-only `test_duplicate_detection.py`: opening the comparison (double-click on a card) and the automatic return to the grid, dissolving a group with ✗ (persistent, does not affect other groups), the duplicates popup opened from the viewer button, deleting one copy → `duplicate_group_id` goes back to `NULL` on the last member, and the "Duplicate status…" dialog (View the groups / Check now / Close). |
| `test_edit_nondestructive.py` | Brightness adjustment through the real UI (`LuminositeTreatmentDialog`) → persisted in `edits.db` → Ctrl+Z ("Undo" button) → undo persisted → navigating back to the same photo → confirmation that the state really comes back from the DB (not just from memory). |
| `test_edit_treatments_extended.py` | Contrast/Colors/Straighten/Vignette (plain slider, direct persistence in `edits.db`), Rotation/Mirror H/Mirror V (direct buttons), Reset (the whole `photo_edits` row is removed), and above all the **priority regression** of the historical `GammaCurveWidget` `NameError` (commit `34d8c5e`): actually ticking "Advanced options…" then "Expert options…" in the Brightness dialog to trigger its `paintEvent` under real conditions. |
| `test_export.py` | Edit + export (from the viewer) → the resulting `.jpg` really bakes in the edit (measured as a mean-luminance delta) and keeps the original file's dates (`preserve_file_dates`). |
| `test_export_extended.py` | The second entry point of the export (multi-selection in the grid, not the viewer), at least two contrasting size presets ("Small" resizes, "Medium" does not, on this synthetic library), and the anti-collision naming `{stem}_1.jpg` when re-exporting into the same folder. |
| `test_folder_management.py` | Full life cycle of a watched folder: `FolderManagerDialog` (forced rescan with a real observable effect, "Remove" — files untouched on disk, catalog rows purged), sidebar tree (create/rename/delete a subfolder — the rename is checked against both `catalog.db` AND `faces.db`, the only case where both `update_paths_prefix` are exercised together end to end). |
| `test_albums.py` | The three album-creation paths (sidebar "+", "Create a new album with…" on a grid multi-selection, "Add … to an album…" on a single selection) and the single deletion path (sidebar context menu, standard Yes/No confirmation) — checks the `albums`/`album_photos` rows without ever touching the photos or the files on disk. |
| `test_save_options_and_settings.py` | "Save the edited image to disk" (overwrite + `.tmp_originals` backup), the "Do not ask again" checkbox in the delete confirmation (persisted as `ui.delete_no_confirm`), External applications (viewer icon added then removed), Settings › Video player (`config.json` round-trip), Help/About. |
| `test_sidebar_special_views.py` | Special sidebar views (Favorites, Videos, filename search) — end-to-end proof of the two favorites fixes from this effort (a viewer that persisted nothing, a grid menu item with no callback), through both entry points (viewer button + grid context menu). |
| `test_faces_identify_and_reset.py` | Uses `isolated_app_with_faces` (7 face photos, see `fixtures/faces/`). `test_faces_identify_and_reset`: identify an isolated face (new person) and a whole cluster (new person) from the viewer/`FaceClusterGrid`, merge the two people created, ignore then restore a face, "Reset the groups only" (RESET_CLUSTERING, non-destructive — identified people must survive). `test_faces_reset_full` (run separately, destructive): "Full reset" (RESET_FULL) → `faces`/`indexed_photos` emptied then fully reindexed — a direct regression test for the stale HDBSCAN clustering-cache bug (`clusterer._last_clustered_n`) fixed in 2026-07 (see `bugfix_clustering_cache_stale_after_reset_2026-07.md`). |

The exact steps of each file are documented in its own module docstring — this
table is deliberately kept as a summary.

## Synchronisation mechanism: poll the DBs, not the UI

`ThumbnailGrid` is hand-painted (no native text UIA can use for its cells) and
the long operations (scan, duplicate detection, face indexing) have no reliable
UI marker to wait on. The **primary** synchronisation mechanism is therefore
`wait_for_condition()` (`tests/e2e/conftest.py`), which polls `catalog.db`/
`edits.db` directly through `query_one()` — a real read-only
`sqlite3.connect()`, running alongside the application process that writes to
the same file.

`wait_for_log()` (tailing `logs/pixelphotomanager.log` from an offset captured
with `log_offset()`) is provided as a fallback for events that leave no trace
in a database.

## Targeting specific UIA elements

- **Native buttons / dialogs** (`QMessageBox`, `QDialog` buttons):
  `find_dialog_button(window, texts, exact=False)`. Established empirically
  during that session: Qt `QDialog`/`QMessageBox` on Windows appear as
  **descendants** of the main window in the UIA tree (owned windows), never as
  separate top-level windows — never use `app.window(title=...)` to target
  them, always `window.descendants(...)`.
- **Specific thumbnails**: `find_thumbnail(window, photo_path)`, which relies
  on the accessible name `thumb::<path>` deliberately set on `ThumbnailCell`
  (`src/ui/thumbnail_grid.py::_setup_ui`) — the only reliable way to target a
  given thumbnail in the hand-painted virtual grid.
- **Sliders** (`EditSlider` → `MarkedSlider` → the real `QSlider`):
  `window.descendants(control_type="Slider")` + `.set_value(int(v * 100))`
  (the internal scale of `EditSlider` is always ×100).
- **Text fields** (e.g. the export destination folder):
  `window.descendants(control_type="Edit")`, disambiguated by the **content**
  of the field rather than by position (several `QLineEdit` can coexist on
  screen, e.g. the EXIF panel while the viewer is open).

## Adding a scenario

1. New file in `scenarios/`, with `pytestmark = pytest.mark.e2e` at the top.
2. The `isolated_app` fixture (function-scoped — a fresh application process
   and a dedicated copy of the synthetic library per test, so that destructive
   scenarios — deletion, moving — do not pollute the others) gives access to
   `.window` (pywinauto), `.manifest` (`LibraryManifest`), `.catalog_db`,
   `.edits_db`, `.faces_db`. For a scenario that needs real face photos, use
   `isolated_app_with_faces` instead (same attributes, plus `.face_photos`);
   for a non-default starting config state, parametrise `isolated_app`
   indirectly (see its docstring in `conftest.py`).
3. Always check state through the DBs (`query_one`/`wait_for_condition`)
   rather than through the text shown on screen — more robust, and it is the
   application's real source of truth.
4. Never click "blind" on guessed screen coordinates: go through
   `find_dialog_button`/`find_thumbnail`/`descendants(control_type=...)`.

## Known limits / accepted debt

- E2e coverage of face identification/merging/reset now exists
  (`test_faces_identify_and_reset.py`, dedicated `isolated_app_with_faces`
  fixture + `tests/e2e/fixtures/faces/`, 7 images: 3 solo "Person A", 3 solo
  "Person B", 1 photo of both together, generated/chosen so as not to depict
  any identifiable real person). No assumption is made about the exact
  topology of the HDBSCAN clustering (not guaranteed reproducible on
  AI-generated faces): each step queries `faces.db` to find a candidate rather
  than guessing an id or a number of groups.
- Deliberately out of scope for this effort: any automation of a drag or
  freehand gesture on a hand-painted widget (cropping, vignette handles,
  red-eye placement, annotations, white-balance eyedropper, manual face bbox,
  thumbnail drag-and-drop) — judged too fragile under UIA for the value it
  would bring. The native Windows picker
  (`QFileDialog.getExistingDirectory`/`getOpenFileName`, e.g. "Add a folder…",
  "Move to…", "Save to another location…") is not automated either: it is a
  Shell window separate from the application's UIA tree, same reasoning.
- `test_scan_and_browse.py::test_scan_reports_corrupted_file_as_repairable_or_skipped`
  does not pin down the exact fate of the corrupted file (catalogued with an
  error vs. skipped) — that depends on `file_repair.py`, which this scenario
  does not yet specify.
- Known flakiness: focus stealing by native Windows dialogs if another window
  has focus at the moment of the click; UIA can take a few hundred ms to
  expose a newly displayed control (hence the retry loops in every `find_*`
  helper rather than direct lookups).
